entities.name: Will Steger
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Will Steger, born in Richfield, Minnesota, on August 27, 1944, emerged as a preeminent American polar explorer and environmental advocate whose pioneering dogsled expeditions redefined the limits of human endurance and significantly amplified public awareness regarding the fragility of Earth's polar regions. His career, spanning from the late 20th century into the present, uniquely melds audacious physical achievement with urgent ecological messaging, establishing him as a crucial voice in the global climate change discourse and a living link to the golden age of polar exploration.

Steger's formidable achievements include the first confirmed dogsled journey to the North Pole in 1986, a monumental 56-day, 1,000-mile odyssey across shifting ice. Two years later, in 1988, he led the 1,600-mile south–north traverse of Greenland, then the longest unsupported dogsled expedition in history, showcasing unparalleled logistical planning and resilience. His most globally impactful feat was the historic 3,471-mile International Trans-Antarctic Expedition (1989–90), the first dogsled traverse of Antarctica, which brought together a six-person international team and captivated millions worldwide, providing an unprecedented platform to discuss the continent's environmental threats.

Beyond his expeditions, Steger's legacy is firmly rooted in his tireless environmental advocacy. He founded the Steger International Polar Project (now Climate Generation: A Will Steger Legacy) in 1991, an organization dedicated to educating and empowering individuals to engage in solutions to climate change. His work has shifted the public perception of polar regions from remote, exotic locales to critical barometers of global environmental health, influencing policy discussions and inspiring countless individuals to confront the climate crisis.

His work directly contributed to shifting the narrative around polar regions from remote wilderness to critical indicators of planetary health.
